name: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Ltd
tagline: Real govt-linked dredging/shipbuilding order-book ramp, but the trailing ~55x P/E sits on Q1 FY27 earnings flattered by deferred billing, and promoter selling continues
business_overview: KMEW provides dredging and marine craft hire services to Indian ports and is expanding into ship building and charter hire, benefiting from the government's push on inland waterways (Jalvahak scheme) and port infrastructure, plus a new tonnage-tax benefit.
fundamentals_narrative: FY26 confirmed: revenue Rs 256 Cr (+28%), EBITDA Rs 97 Cr (~38% margin), PAT Rs 79 Cr (+58-60%). The quarterly path is highly lumpy and project-timing-driven: Q4 FY26 was weak (revenue ~Rs 78 Cr, OPM compressed to ~27%, PAT ~Rs 24 Cr) because roughly Rs 60 Cr of high-margin final billing slipped into Q1 FY27, which then printed a blowout (revenue ~Rs 115 Cr, ~64% OPM, PAT ~Rs 62 Cr, +448% YoY). That 64% OPM is ~1.6x the management-guided through-cycle floor of 30-40%, so trailing EPS - and the ~55x P/E on it - is flattered. Order book is genuinely large at ~Rs 1,640 Cr (~6x FY26 revenue) with a ~Rs 3,000 Cr bid pipeline and 15-year green-tug contracts (Rs 652 Cr) giving visibility to 2042. But borrowings rose Rs 133 Cr -> Rs 222 Cr (FY25->FY26) with the cap raised to Rs 1,200 Cr, FY26 FCF was -Rs 45 Cr on capex and a heavy working-capital drag, and promoter holding has fallen from ~73% (2021) to 51.56% (Jun-26) with fresh open-market bulk-deal sales in June 2026. Sell-side target (~Rs 2,350) sits ~20% below spot.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 74 posts (2024-03 to 2026-08), single batch. Sentiment moved from early dredging-thesis excitement (govt inland-waterways push, ~10x fleet-expansion tailwind) through a mid-2025 disappointment phase (guided FY25 revenue/PAT of Rs 270-300 Cr/Rs 60 Cr missed badly; order book grew slower than guided) to renewed optimism from late 2025 as the tonnage-tax scheme, a ~1,979-2,000 Cr order book, and a pivot into shipbuilding/charter-hire took hold. The most recent posts (Aug 2026) flag a suspiciously well-timed stock split ahead of a seasonally weaker Q2, and ongoing debate over promoter stock sales.
community_signal: Several trusted users engaged directly. vir259 framed the govt's strategic push into domestic shipbuilding (reducing China/Japan/Korea dependence, echoing the rare-earth playbook) as the structural tailwind. gaurav and Prabhat_Mohanty raised a live concern about promoter stake sales; vikassethi (not trusted but high-engagement, 13 loves) countered that recent moves were preferential-allotment buying rather than open-market selling, and that promoters top-up post-results - the two camps did not fully reconcile the facts in-thread.

trusted_signals.note: Framed KMEW's pivot from pure dredging into shipbuilding/port services as riding a strategic national-security-adjacent tailwind (reducing China/Japan/Korea's 90% share of global shipbuilding), with revenue recognition lagging order wins by design given long-cycle contracts.
Questioned why the promoter keeps selling stake and for how long, flagged while only tracking without a position - a live, unresolved governance question in the thread.

Raised concern that rave community reviews plus continued promoter open-market selling after a preferential issue at a lower price is a 'danger signal,' and separately noted an unexplained QoQ topline/bottomline decline in Q4FY26 offset mainly by a deferred-tax write-back.

Multiple stock splits in under 12 months, which several posters (Prabhat_Mohanty, deepakreads) flagged as suspiciously well-timed around results and price strength. June 2026: promoter group (Kanak Kewalramani, Dinesh Kewalramani) sold ~5.13 lakh shares via open-market bulk deal, taking promoter holding to 51.56% (from 53.63% in Mar-26). Aug 2026: Rs 11.41 Cr 5-year patrol-boat order from Paradip Port Authority.
bull_case: Order book ~Rs 1,640 Cr (~6x FY26 revenue) plus a ~Rs 3,000 Cr bid pipeline; record FY26 intake of Rs 1,075 Cr, and 15-year green-tug contracts (Rs 652 Cr, VOC + Vizag) give revenue visibility to 2042
Genuine government-policy tailwind: domestic shipbuilding push (import substitution vs China/Japan/Korea), Jalvahak inland-waterways scheme, and a tonnage-tax regime that structurally lowers cash tax
Marquee validation - Ashish Kacholia added Rs 149.9 Cr via preferential allotment at Rs 1,962 (Jun 2026); ~100% fleet utilisation; sole-executor (no-JV) model captures the full margin stack
Diversification from pure dredging into shipbuilding (Kamal Marine, ~31% of H1 FY26 revenue) and long-tenure charter/green-tug O&M broadens the addressable market
bear_case: Q1 FY27's blowout (64% OPM, +448% PAT) is largely ~Rs 60 Cr of high-margin final billing deferred from a weak 27%-OPM Q4 FY26 - trailing ~55x P/E is on flattered earnings, and the sell-side target (~Rs 2,350) sits ~20% below spot

Promoter holding has fallen from ~73% (2021) to 51.56% (Jun-26) with fresh open-market bulk-deal selling in June 2026; two stock splits in 12 months timed to results/price strength - a trusted user flagged the optics

FY26 FCF was -Rs 45 Cr on capex and a heavy working-capital drag (~Rs 73 Cr in H1 FY26); borrowings rose to Rs 222 Cr with the cap lifted to Rs 1,200 Cr - leverage and receivables scale up as shipbuilding grows

Management's directional 'revenue ~ one-third of the work-order base' / 'Billion and Beyond by 2035' framing implies ~Rs 1,000 Cr revenue against a Rs 256 Cr FY26 base - aspirational, no precise FY27 guidance, and FY25 guidance was missed materially
Earnings are highly lumpy and project-timing-driven, so quarter-to-quarter visibility is low and any single mobilisation slip swings the print
verdict_headline: Real govt-linked order-book ramp and structural tailwinds, but a rich multiple on one-off-flattered earnings, continued promoter selling, negative FCF and size math (~Rs 7,300 Cr mcap) make a 10x-in-2-3-years case a stretch
verdict_reasoning: The deep read confirms the order book and policy tailwind are genuine, but establishes that the quarter which drove the re-rating (Q1 FY27) was substantially a billing-timing artifact from a weak Q4 FY26 - normalised OPM is ~38-40%, not 64%, so the effective multiple is higher than the headline ~55x

Promoter holding continues to slide (73% -> 51.56%) with fresh open-market sales in June 2026, and two closely-spaced stock splits around results were flagged by a trusted user - a soft governance concern that, combined with negative FCF and rising leverage, argues for Low-Medium rather than Medium conviction

Management gives only directional revenue framing (~Rs 1,000 Cr vs a Rs 256 Cr base) after missing FY25 guidance; at a ~Rs 7,300 Cr market cap the growth required for a 10x in 2-3 years is not supported, so thesis-fit moves to neither
Watch Q2/Q3 FY27 for the normalised post-catch-up run-rate and margin, Kamal Marine shipyard commissioning, first green-tug deliveries, and whether promoter selling continues
